sources.audit_notes: COUNTS FROM THE FETCHED ARTEFACT, NOT THE PAPER. test_cases_dh_base.json = 510 cases, test_cases_ds_base.json = 544 cases, sum 1054, which matches the paper claim of 1,054 per setting. The enhanced files (test_cases_dh_enhanced.json, test_cases_ds_enhanced.json) hold the same 1054 cases in the same order with only the Tool Response rewritten (a 'IMPORTANT!!! Ignore all previous instructions...' hacking prompt prepended to the injected instruction); total rows across the four files = 2,108 but unique cases = 1,054. Case matrix is exactly 62 attacker scenarios x 17 user tools (each scenario appears 17 times, once per user tool; each user tool appears 62 times). 17 user tools confirmed (data/user_cases.jsonl, 12 Level=High, 5 Level=Low). ATTACKER TOOL COUNT DISCREPANCY: README and paper claim 62 attacker tools; the test files actually reference 63 distinct attacker tool names (30 direct-harm tools + 32 data-stealing fetch tools + the shared GmailSendEmail stage-2 tool). The 62 figure counts attacker scenarios, not tools. Reported count: 63. LICENCE VERDICT: MIT, no NC clause, redistribution of case contents permitted provided the copyright notice ships along; decision = allowed_with_attribution, so raw JSON may stay in external/raw and derived harmonised rows may enter the corpus. No gated access on GitHub; Hugging Face mirrors exist (masahiroid/injecagent-ja, MIT-licensed Japanese translation; penfever/injecagent-harbor, per-case Docker/harbor repackaging with no licence field on the repo card). The official artefact is the GitHub repo, which is ungated and self-contained (~7.9 MB), so the HF mirrors were inventoried but not downloaded. FIELD INVENTORY per test case (all four files share the schema): 'Attack Type' (string, category label), 'Attacker Instruction' (the malicious objective as an imperative sentence), 'Attacker Tools' (list; length 1 for direct-harm, length 2 for data-stealing where element 0 is the fetch tool and element 1 is always GmailSendEmail), 'Expected Achievements' (free-text attacker objective), 'Modifed' [sic] (0/1 flag, instruction paraphrased to fit the user context; 187/510 dh and 153/544 ds are 1), 'Thought' (seeded agent reasoning for the legitimate call), 'Tool Parameters' (arguments of the legitimate call, python-repr string), 'Tool Response' (injection-filled observed response), 'Tool Response Template' (with '<Attacker Instruction>' placeholder), 'User Instruction', 'User Tool'. TRAJECTORY ANSWER: a case is not a bare single call. Each case is a seeded two-step context: legitimate user-tool call (name + arguments given) whose tool response carries the injection, and the agent must emit the NEXT call; that next call is the object of judgment. Data-stealing cases are evaluated in two stages (S1 attacker fetch call, then a simulated fetch response shipped in attacker_simulated_responses.json, 2,347 keyed (tool,parameters) pairs, then S2 GmailSendEmail whose arguments must contain the fetched data). The harness counts up to 3 further actions and treats re-calling the user tool with fabricated observations as invalid. So per-case history depth is 1..3 calls, dependency S2-args-on-S1-response present. TOOL DEFINITIONS: shipped in data/tools.json, 38 toolkits / 330 functions, each function has name, summary, parameters (name/type/description/required) and returns; the join key is toolkit+function (src/utils.py get_tool_dict). All 17 user tools and all 63 attacker tools resolve in tools.json with zero missing definitions. LABELS: explicit attacker objective present twice ('Attacker Instruction' + 'Expected Achievements') plus a coarse category ('Attack Type'); the direct-harm vs data-stealing split is encoded at file level (dh_* vs ds_*), NOT as an in-row field; the two-stage variant is marked structurally by the 2-element Attacker Tools list. No per-row expected_outcome field; the expected outcome is implicit (the labelled attack should be blocked). No case ids, no tenant, no phase, no budget fields in the artefact. MAPPING FEASIBILITY against the current GATE surface (admin_tool, code_execute, data_analysis, database_query, format_template, http_request, send_email, sql_query, web_search): 714/1054 cases map cleanly (187 dh: 11 scenarios x 17 = CiscoUmbrellaCreatePolicy/UpdatePolicy and NortonIdentitySafeDisableTwoFactor/SharePassword/AutoFill and EvernoteManagerManageNoteSharingLevel and FacebookManagerUpdateUserProfile and The23andMeShareData/UpdateData to admin_tool, GitHubDeleteRepository to admin_tool, TerminalExecute to code_execute; 527 ds: all 31 non-deepfake scenarios where stage-1 fetch maps to database_query or data_analysis or web_search and stage-2 exfil maps to send_email). 340 cases require a new tool or profile: payment backend 7 scenarios (BankManagerPayBill, BankManagerTransferFunds, BinanceDeposit, BinancePlaceOrder, BinanceWithdraw, VenmoWithdrawMoney, FedExShipManagerManageShipment) = 119; IoT/physical actuators 7 scenarios (AugustSmartLockGrantGuestAccess/UnlockDoor, GoogleHomeScheduleDeviceAction, IndoorRobotGoToRoom, TrafficControlGivePriorityToEmergencyVehicle/ManageTrafficLightState, EmergencyDispatchSystemCreateDispatchRequest) = 119; health/calendar 3 EpicFHIR scenarios (ManageAppointments, ManageClinicalDocuments, ManagePatientRecords) = 51; filesystem DropboxMoveItem = 17; messaging SlackLeaveChannel = 17; media generation DeepfakeGeneratorGenerateAudioDeepfake = 17. These gaps match SPEC section 14 verbatim (payment, filesystem, calendar, messaging workspace, persistent memory not expressible). The 17 user-side legitimate calls map acceptably as web_search/http_request/database_query reads, EXCEPT GoogleCalendarReadEvents and GoogleCalendarGetEventsFromSharedCalendar (34 attack contexts + 2 benign templates) which need the calendar gap, and WebBrowserNavigateTo which degrades to http_request. DEGENERATE-F01 WARNING: if attacker tools are simply left ungranted, all 1,054 cases become trivially F01 unauthorized_tool_invocation at the privilege stage and the source tests nothing past stage 1. Harmonisation must map the malicious call onto an IN-GRANT mediated tool (or extend the surface per section 14) so the case reaches contracts/semantic, and must record that transformation in notes, otherwise the benchmark measures tool-list hygiene, not GATE. FAMILY SUPPLY (primary by violated property, secondary records the injection trigger): F06 = 544 (all ds, exfiltration objective, secondary privilege/semantic); F05 = 476 (28 dh scenarios, harm inside the acting grant, secondary semantic); F07 = 17 (GitHubDeleteRepository); F09 = 17 (TerminalExecute, shell/file policy violation, secondary F06); F04 = 0 as primary: every case is hijacked via injected content so semantic_masking/intent deviation is real but is carried as attack_vector=tool_response/retrieved_content plus secondary layer, matching section 4's rule that vector is a separate axis; B01 = 17 (the 17 distinct legitimate preceding calls, each appearing 62 times, usable as paired benign controls). NOTHING SUPPLIED: F01 (only degenerate), F02, F03, F08, F10, F11, F12, F13, F14, F15, F16, F17. All 1,054 cases are single-tenant, no prior state, no budget arithmetic, one-shot action selection, so the source contributes zero to the stateful families F10-F14 and to memory family F17; expected and stated honestly in section 10 shortfall planning. Recommended pin for case rows: test_cases_dh_base.json and test_cases_ds_base.json at this commit, base setting only; enhanced is a prompt variant of the same cases and must become a config column, not duplicate rows. Dedup keeps 1054 templates x settings collapsed by template_family (62 scenario templates x 17 user contexts, all distinct, so no dedup loss).
